polity.zh: 罗马附庸国 / 罗马犹地亚

name.zh: 伊利亚 / 圣城（古德斯）

polity.zh: 历代哈里发国（正统、倭马亚、阿拔斯、法蒂玛）
阿尤布王朝、马穆鲁克王朝
以色列控制；国际地位存在争议

summary.en: A city sacred to Judaism, Christianity and Islam. Hadrian refounded it as Aelia Capitolina after 135; Arabic usage moved from Iliya to al-Quds ("the Holy"). Its sovereignty, especially of East Jerusalem, remains disputed between Israel and the Palestinians.
summary.zh: 犹太教、基督教和伊斯兰教共同的圣城。135年后哈德良将其重建为爱利亚加比多连；阿拉伯语称谓由“伊利亚”逐渐变为“古德斯”（意为“神圣”）。其主权，尤其是东耶路撒冷的地位，至今仍是以色列与巴勒斯坦之间的争议焦点。

note: Frankish rule briefly returned in 1229–1244; not shown as a separate span.

polity.zh: 伊利汗国、札剌亦儿王朝、土库曼诸王朝、萨法维王朝

polity.en: British occupation and Mandate; Kingdom of Iraq from 1921
polity.zh: 英国占领与委任统治；1921年起为伊拉克王国

summary.en: Founded by al-Mansur in 762 as the round city of Madinat al-Salam near an older village called Baghdad. Capital of the Abbasid caliphate until the Mongol sack of 1258, then a provincial centre under Ilkhanid, Safavid and Ottoman rule, and capital of Iraq since 1921.
summary.zh: 762年由曼苏尔在名为“巴格达”的旧村附近建为圆城“和平之城”。在1258年蒙古攻陷前一直是阿拔斯王朝首都，此后在伊利汗国、萨法维和奥斯曼治下为地方中心，1921年起为伊拉克首都。

sources.title: J. Lassner, The Topography of Baghdad in the Early Middle Ages (1970)

note: Safavid control in 1508–1534 and 1624–1638 is folded into the adjacent spans.

polity.zh: 哈里发国、布韦希、塞尔柱（首都）、伊利汗国、帖木儿

polity.en: Hotaki, Afsharid, Zand and Qajar Iran
polity.zh: 霍塔克、阿夫沙尔、赞德与卡扎尔伊朗

summary.en: Known in antiquity as Aspadana and to the Sasanians as Spahan, the city was a Seljuk capital and reached its height after Shah Abbas I made it the Safavid capital in 1598, until the Afghan conquest of 1722.
summary.zh: 古称阿斯帕达纳，萨珊时期称斯帕汉，曾为塞尔柱王朝都城；1598年阿拔斯一世定都于此后达到鼎盛，直至1722年阿富汗人攻陷。

note: The identification of ancient Aspadana/Gabae with Isfahan is generally accepted but approximate.

polity.zh: 第比利斯埃米尔国（哈里发治下）

polity.en: Kingdom of Georgia; Kartli and Kartli-Kakheti
polity.zh: 格鲁吉亚王国；卡特利及卡特利-卡赫季王国
格鲁吉亚苏维埃社会主义共和国
格鲁吉亚苏维埃社会主义共和国

summary.en: Founded by King Vakhtang Gorgasali in the 5th century near hot springs (Georgian tbili, "warm"). Under Arab emirs for four centuries, it was retaken by David IV in 1122. The Russian form Tiflis was officially replaced by Tbilisi in 1936.
summary.zh: 5世纪由瓦赫坦·戈尔加萨利国王在温泉附近建立（格鲁吉亚语tbili意为“温暖”）。阿拉伯埃米尔统治约四百年后，1122年被大卫四世收复。俄语名称“梯弗里斯”于1936年正式改为“第比利斯”。

sources.title: D. Rayfield, Edge of Empires: A History of Georgia (2012)

note: Founding c. 455–479 is traditional; capital status shifted between Tbilisi and other towns at times.

polity.zh: 罗马帝国（加拉太行省首府）

polity.en: Seljuks of Rum and Turkish beyliks
polity.zh: 罗姆塞尔柱及突厥诸侯国

summary.en: Ancient Ancyra, capital of the Roman province of Galatia and site of the Monumentum Ancyranum. Under the Ottomans it was known in the West as Angora, famous for its goats' wool. Atatürk made it the base of the national movement in 1920 and the capital of the Republic in 1923.
summary.zh: 古称安基拉，罗马加拉太行省首府，存有《奥古斯都功业录》铭文。奥斯曼时期在西方称安哥拉，以安哥拉山羊毛著称。1920年阿塔图尔克以此为民族运动基地，1923年定为共和国首都。

sources.title: C. Foss, "Late Antique and Byzantine Ankara", Dumbarton Oaks Papers 31 (1977)

note: Turkish control after 1073 was interrupted; the date of Ottoman capture (1354) follows the usual account. Western use of "Angora" ended after the 1930 postal law.

polity.en: Aydınid beylik (harbour castle held by the Knights Hospitaller 1344–1402)
polity.zh: 艾登侯国（港口城堡1344—1402年由医院骑士团据守）

summary.en: Ancient Smyrna was one of the great ports of Roman Asia and an early Christian centre. Contested between Turkish emirs, Byzantines and crusading knights, it became Ottoman in the 15th century and a cosmopolitan trading city; it was occupied by Greece in 1919 and largely burned in 1922.
summary.zh: 古城士麦那是罗马亚细亚行省的大港之一和早期基督教中心。曾在突厥埃米尔、拜占庭和十字军骑士之间反复易手，15世纪归入奥斯曼，成为多元的贸易城市；1919年被希腊占领，1922年大部分毁于大火。

sources.title: P. Mansel, Levant: Splendour and Catastrophe on the Mediterranean (2010)

note: Byzantine rule was interrupted by the emir Tzachas (c. 1081–1097); Ottoman control was definitive from c. 1426.

polity.zh: 本都王国 / 罗马帝国

summary.en: A Greek colony on the Black Sea, Trapezus was a Roman port and later a Byzantine stronghold. From 1204 it was capital of the Komnenian Empire of Trebizond, the last Byzantine successor state, until Mehmed II took it in 1461.
summary.zh: 黑海沿岸的希腊殖民城市特拉佩祖斯，曾为罗马港口和拜占庭要塞。1204年起为科穆宁家族特拉比松帝国的首都，这是最后一个拜占庭继承国，1461年被穆罕默德二世攻占。

sources.title: A. Bryer, The Empire of Trebizond and the Pontos (1980)

note: Pontus was annexed to Rome in stages (64 CE for eastern Pontus).

polity.zh: 罗马帝国（叙利亚行省首府）
历代哈里发国与哈姆丹王朝
法国委任统治（亚历山大勒塔区）

summary.en: Founded by Seleucus I around 300 BCE, Antioch was one of the largest cities of the Roman East and the place where followers of Jesus were first called Christians. Repeatedly ruined by earthquakes and wars, it was a crusader principality capital and joined Turkey in 1939.
summary.zh: 约公元前300年由塞琉古一世建立，安条克是罗马东方最大的城市之一，耶稣的追随者在此首次被称为“基督徒”。屡遭地震和战乱摧残，曾为十字军安条克公国首都，1939年并入土耳其。

sources.title: G. Downey, A History of Antioch in Syria from Seleucus to the Arab Conquest (1961)

polity.zh: 历代哈里发国及埃米尔国

polity.en: Zengids, Ayyubids, Mongols, Mamluks, Aq Qoyunlu
polity.zh: 赞吉、阿尤布、蒙古、马穆鲁克、白羊王朝

summary.en: Edessa, capital of the kingdom of Osroene, was a cradle of Syriac Christianity. Its Arabic name al-Ruha comes from the Syriac Urhay, the root of modern Urfa. It was the first crusader state (1098–1144), and received the honorific "Şanlı" (glorious) in 1984.
summary.zh: 埃德萨是奥斯若恩王国都城，也是叙利亚语基督教的摇篮。阿拉伯语名“鲁哈”源于叙利亚语“乌尔海”，也是今名“乌尔法”的来源。它是第一个十字军国家（1098—1144年）的中心，1984年获“尚勒”（光荣）称号。

sources.title: J. B. Segal, Edessa: "The Blessed City" (1970)

note: End of Osroene's independence is dated variously 214–242; Sasanian occupation 609–628 is not shown.

name.en: Nineveh area (Ninwe; fortress opposite the ruins)
name.zh: 尼尼微一带（尼尼微遗址对岸的要塞）

polity.zh: 历代哈里发国、哈姆丹、乌盖勒、塞尔柱
伊利汗国及其后继王朝

polity.en: British occupation and Mandate of Iraq
polity.zh: 英国占领与伊拉克委任统治

summary.en: Mosul grew on the west bank of the Tigris opposite the ruins of Assyrian Nineveh. Taken by the Arabs in 641, it flourished as a Zengid capital and trading centre, gave its name to muslin, and was held by ISIS in 2014–2017.
summary.zh: 摩苏尔位于底格里斯河西岸，与亚述古都尼尼微遗址隔河相望。641年被阿拉伯人攻占，曾作为赞吉王朝都城和商贸中心而繁荣，“平纹细布”（muslin）一词即源于其名；2014—2017年被“伊斯兰国”占据。

note: The pre-Islamic settlement and its name are poorly documented; the first span is approximate.

polity.zh: 伊利汗国及其后继王朝
萨法维、阿夫沙尔与赞德伊朗

summary.en: A village near the great city of Rey, Tehran grew after the Mongols destroyed Rey in 1220. Shah Tahmasp I walled it in the 16th century, and Agha Mohammad Khan Qajar made it his capital; it has been the capital of Iran ever since.
summary.zh: 德黑兰原是大城剌夷附近的村落，1220年蒙古人毁灭剌夷后逐渐兴起。16世纪塔赫玛斯普一世为其筑城墙，阿迦·穆罕默德汗·卡扎尔定都于此，此后一直是伊朗首都。

note: Capital from 1786 per most sources; Wikidata gives 1794 as an inception-type date.

modern.zh: 萨勒曼帕克（泰西封遗址）

polity.zh: 正统、倭马亚与阿拔斯哈里发国
阿拔斯王朝及后继诸国

summary.en: Twin city on the Tigris, with Seleucia opposite, that served as the Parthian and Sasanian capital. The Arabs called the conurbation al-Mada'in; it declined after Baghdad was founded. The great arch of the Taq-i Kisra still stands at Salman Pak, named after the companion Salman al-Farisi.
summary.zh: 泰西封与对岸的塞琉西亚组成底格里斯河畔的双城，是安息和萨珊的都城。阿拉伯人称这一城市群为“麦达因”，巴格达建立后逐渐衰落。著名的霍斯劳拱门至今矗立在以圣门弟子萨勒曼·法尔西命名的萨勒曼帕克。

note: The modern name Salman Pak predates Iraqi independence; the 1932 boundary only marks the state change.

polity.zh: 阿拔斯、图伦、伊赫什德、法蒂玛
塞尔柱、布里德、赞吉、阿尤布

summary.en: One of the oldest continuously inhabited cities in the world. Damascus was the Umayyad capital from 661 to 750 and later a major centre under the Ayyubids, Mamluks and Ottomans, and has been the capital of independent Syria since 1946.
summary.zh: 世界上有人持续居住的最古老城市之一。661—750年为倭马亚王朝首都，后在阿尤布、马穆鲁克和奥斯曼治下仍是重要中心，1946年起为独立叙利亚的首都。

sources.title: R. Burns, Damascus: A History (2nd ed., 2019)

polity.en: Caliphates; Sharifate of Mecca from c. 967
polity.zh: 历代哈里发国；约967年起为麦加谢里夫国
奥斯曼宗主下的谢里夫国

summary.en: A caravan and pilgrimage town around the Kaaba, birthplace of Muhammad and the holiest city of Islam. Governed for nearly a millennium by sharifs descended from the Prophet under successive overlords, it passed to the Saudis in 1924–25.
summary.zh: 围绕克尔白形成的商队与朝觐城镇，穆罕默德的出生地，伊斯兰教第一圣城。近一千年间由先知后裔谢里夫在历代宗主国之下治理，1924—1925年归入沙特。

sources.title: F. E. Peters, Mecca: A Literary History of the Muslim Holy Land (1994)

note: Mecca's pre-Islamic history is poorly documented; the first span starts at an approximate date.

polity.en: Armenian kingdoms and successive Persian, Arab and Turkic rulers
polity.zh: 亚美尼亚诸王国及历代波斯、阿拉伯、突厥统治者

polity.en: Safavid and later Persian rule (Erivan Khanate), with Ottoman interludes
polity.zh: 萨法维及其后波斯统治（埃里温汗国），间有奥斯曼统治
亚美尼亚苏维埃社会主义共和国

summary.en: Yerevan traces its origin to the Urartian fortress of Erebuni, founded by King Argishti I in 782 BCE. A modest town for centuries, it was the seat of the Persian khans of Erivan until Russia took it in 1827–28, and became capital of Armenia in 1918.
summary.zh: 埃里温起源于公元前782年乌拉尔图国王阿尔吉什提一世修建的埃里布尼要塞。数百年间规模不大，曾为波斯埃里温汗的治所，1827—1828年被俄国占领，1918年成为亚美尼亚首都。

note: Continuity between Erebuni and medieval Erevan is assumed; the long second span lumps many rulers.

summary.en: Nicaea hosted the first (325) and seventh (787) ecumenical councils. It was briefly the first capital of the Seljuks of Rum, the seat of the Byzantine government-in-exile after 1204, and under the Ottomans became famous for İznik pottery and tiles.
summary.zh: 尼西亚曾召开第一次（325年）和第七次（787年）大公会议。它一度是罗姆塞尔柱的首个都城，1204年后为拜占庭流亡政府所在地，奥斯曼时期以伊兹尼克陶器和瓷砖闻名。

sources.title: C. Foss, Nicaea: A Byzantine Capital and Its Praises (1996)

polity.zh: 历代哈里发国、拉瓦德、塞尔柱、伊尔迪吉兹
札剌亦儿、黑羊、白羊王朝

polity.en: Safavid, Afsharid, Zand and Qajar Iran (seat of the crown prince under the Qajars)
polity.zh: 萨法维、阿夫沙尔、赞德与卡扎尔伊朗（卡扎尔时为王储驻地）

summary.en: The main city of Iranian Azerbaijan and a hub of the Silk Road. Tabriz was the Ilkhanid capital, then capital of the Turkmen dynasties and of the early Safavids until the court moved to Qazvin, and a cradle of the Constitutional Revolution.
summary.zh: 伊朗阿塞拜疆的首要城市和丝绸之路枢纽。大不里士曾为伊利汗国都城，后为土库曼诸王朝和早期萨法维王朝的首都，直至宫廷迁往加兹温；它也是立宪革命的摇篮之一。

sources.title: Leiden University, Iran–Turan: Sultaniyya (dedicated as Ilkhanid capital 1313)

note: The Safavid move to Qazvin is dated 1548–1555; Ottoman occupations (e.g. 1585–1603) are not shown. Ilkhanid capital until Öljeitü made Soltaniyeh the capital (dedicated 1313).

summary.en: Iconium, where Paul preached, became Konya, capital of the Seljuk Sultanate of Rum and the city where Rumi taught and is buried. The Ottomans took it in the 1460s, during their long conquest of the Karamanid beylik.
summary.zh: 保罗曾在此传道的以哥念后来成为科尼亚，是罗姆塞尔柱苏丹国的都城，鲁米在此讲学并长眠于此。1460年代，奥斯曼人在逐步征服卡拉曼侯国的过程中夺取该城。

sources.title: C. Cahen, The Formation of Turkey (2001)

note: The Seljuk takeover is dated c. 1084; Konya became the Rum capital after the loss of Nicaea in 1097. Karamanid control after 1308 was intermittent.

polity.zh: 卡帕多细亚王国（罗马附庸）

summary.en: The Cappadocian royal city Mazaca was renamed Caesarea when Tiberius annexed Cappadocia in 17 CE; Basil the Great was its bishop. Turkish speakers turned Kaisareia into Kayseri, a Seljuk caravan hub, and the architect Sinan was born in a nearby village.
summary.zh: 卡帕多细亚王城马扎卡在公元17年提比略吞并该国时改名凯撒利亚，大巴西略曾任此地主教。说突厥语的居民把“凯撒利亚”读成“开塞利”，这里成为塞尔柱时代的商队枢纽，建筑师希南就出生在附近村庄。

note: Turkish conquest c. 1074–1080; the late-medieval sequence of rulers is simplified. Archelaus renamed Mazaca Caesarea c. 12–9 BCE, before Rome annexed Cappadocia in 17 CE.

polity.en: Roman and Byzantine Empires (contested with Persia)
polity.zh: 罗马与拜占庭帝国（与波斯反复争夺）

polity.en: Caliphates, Marwanids, Seljuks, Artuqids, Ayyubids, Mongols
polity.zh: 历代哈里发国、马尔万王朝、塞尔柱、阿尔图格、阿尤布、蒙古
奥斯曼帝国，后为土耳其

summary.en: Ancient Amida on the Tigris, whose black basalt walls withstood and finally fell to Shapur II in 359, as Ammianus Marcellinus witnessed. Its Ottoman name Diyarbekir came from the region ("land of the Bakr" tribe); it was changed to Diyarbakır in 1937. It is the largest Kurdish-majority city in Turkey.
summary.zh: 底格里斯河畔的古城阿米达，其黑色玄武岩城墙在359年被沙普尔二世攻破，阿米亚努斯·马塞利努斯亲历其事。奥斯曼时代的名称“迪亚巴基尔”来自所在地区（“伯克尔部落之地”），1937年改为“迪亚巴克尔”。它是土耳其最大的库尔德人聚居城市。

note: Medieval rulers are compressed into one span.

polity.zh: 正统、倭马亚、阿拔斯哈里发国
法蒂玛、米尔达斯、塞尔柱
赞吉王朝，后为阿尤布王朝

polity.en: Arab Kingdom of Syria, then French Mandate
polity.zh: 叙利亚阿拉伯王国，后为法国委任统治

summary.en: One of the world’s oldest continuously inhabited cities. The Seleucids called it Beroea, but the Semitic name Halab endured. Its citadel, souks and caravanserais made it the Ottoman Levant’s great trading city; much of the old city was devastated in the 2012–16 battle.
summary.zh: 世界上持续有人居住的最古老城市之一。塞琉古王朝称之为贝罗亚，但闪米特语名“哈莱卜”始终沿用。城堡、集市和商队客栈使它成为奥斯曼黎凡特最大的商业城市；2012–2016年的战事使老城大部分遭到毁坏。

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage: Ancient City of Aleppo

polity.en: Emesene client kings, then Roman and Byzantine Empires
polity.zh: 埃梅萨附庸王国，后为罗马与拜占庭帝国
历代哈里发国、哈姆丹、塞尔柱、阿尤布、马穆鲁克

polity.en: Arab Kingdom of Syria, then French Mandate
polity.zh: 叙利亚阿拉伯王国，后为法国委任统治

summary.en: Emesa on the Orontes was home to the sun-god Elagabal, whose priest became the emperor Elagabalus, and to Julia Domna, wife of Septimius Severus. Aurelian beat Zenobia here in 272. As Hims it holds the tomb attributed to Khalid ibn al-Walid.
summary.zh: 奥龙特斯河畔的埃梅萨是太阳神埃拉伽巴尔的圣城，其祭司后来成为罗马皇帝埃拉伽巴路斯，塞普蒂米乌斯·塞维鲁之妻尤利娅·多姆娜也出身于此。272年奥勒良在此击败芝诺比娅。阿拉伯时代称希姆斯，城中有传为哈立德·本·瓦利德的陵墓。

sources.title: Herodian, History of the Empire 5.3 (Emesa and Elagabal)

polity.zh: 历代哈里发国（正统至法蒂玛）

summary.en: A harbour city renamed Ptolemais by the Ptolemies. As Saint-Jean d'Acre it was the capital of the crusader kingdom after 1191, and its fall to the Mamluks in 1291 ended the crusader states. Ahmad al-Jazzar’s walls held off Napoleon in 1799.
summary.zh: 托勒密王朝时改名托勒密城的港口城市。1191年后它以“圣让达克”之名成为十字军王国的首都，1291年被马穆鲁克攻陷，十字军国家随之终结。1799年杰扎尔帕夏修筑的城墙挡住了拿破仑。

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage: Old City of Acre

polity.en: Decapolis under Rome, then Byzantine Empire
polity.zh: 罗马治下的德卡波利斯，后属拜占庭帝国
历代哈里发国、阿尤布、马穆鲁克

polity.en: Ottoman Empire (Circassian settlement from 1878), then Arab Kingdom of Syria
polity.zh: 奥斯曼帝国（1878年起切尔克斯人定居），后为叙利亚阿拉伯王国
外约旦酋长国（英国委任统治）

summary.en: Biblical Rabbath Ammon was refounded as Philadelphia by Ptolemy II and became a Decapolis city with a Roman theatre that still stands. By the 19th century it was a small village resettled by Circassian refugees; Emir Abdullah made it his capital in 1921.
summary.zh: 《圣经》中的拉巴亚扪由托勒密二世重建为费拉德尔菲亚，成为德卡波利斯十城之一，城中罗马剧场保存至今。19世纪时它只是切尔克斯难民重新定居的小村落；1921年阿卜杜拉埃米尔将其定为首都。

sources.title: E. Rogan, Frontiers of the State in the Late Ottoman Empire: Transjordan, 1850–1921 (1999)

polity.zh: 历代哈里发国（正统至法蒂玛）
十字军贝鲁特领地（1187–1197年属阿尤布）

polity.en: Allied occupation, then French Mandate (Greater Lebanon)
polity.zh: 协约国占领，后为法国委任统治（大黎巴嫩）

summary.en: Roman Berytus was famed for its law school until an earthquake and fire destroyed it in 551. It grew into a major Ottoman port in the 19th century, capital of Greater Lebanon under France from 1920 and of independent Lebanon from 1943.
summary.zh: 罗马时代的贝里图斯以法学院闻名，551年毁于地震和大火。19世纪它发展为奥斯曼帝国的重要港口，1920年起为法国治下大黎巴嫩的首府，1943年起为独立黎巴嫩的首都。

sources.title: L. T. Fawaz, Merchants and Migrants in Nineteenth-Century Beirut (1983)

summary.en: Prusa below Mount Olympus (Uludağ) surrendered to Orhan in 1326 after a long blockade and became the first Ottoman capital. The early sultans built their mosques and tombs here, and it grew rich on the silk trade from Iran.
summary.zh: 位于奥林匹斯山（乌卢达格山）脚下的普鲁萨在长期围困后于1326年向奥尔汗投降，成为奥斯曼的第一个首都。早期苏丹在这里兴建清真寺和陵墓，城市借伊朗丝绸贸易而致富。

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage: Bursa and Cumalıkızık: the Birth of the Ottoman Empire

note: The capital moved to Edirne in the 1360s; the exact year (1363–1369) is debated.

polity.en: Caliphate, Shaddadids, Seljuks, Ildegizids, Mongols, Safavids
polity.zh: 哈里发国、沙达德王朝、塞尔柱、伊尔德吉兹、蒙古、萨法维

polity.en: Azerbaijan Democratic Republic, then Soviet Azerbaijan
polity.zh: 阿塞拜疆民主共和国，后为苏维埃阿塞拜疆
阿塞拜疆苏维埃社会主义共和国（苏联）

summary.en: Home of the poet Nizami Ganjavi (12th century). Russia stormed it in 1804 and renamed it Elisavetpol after the empress Elizabeth, wife of Alexander I; it was briefly the seat of the Azerbaijani government in 1918, renamed Kirovabad in 1935, and Ganja again in 1989.
summary.zh: 12世纪诗人内扎米·占贾维的故乡。1804年俄军攻占此城，以亚历山大一世之妻伊丽莎白皇后之名改称伊丽莎白波尔；1918年一度为阿塞拜疆政府驻地，1935年改名基洛瓦巴德，1989年恢复占贾之名。

note: The founding date (9th century, traditionally 859) is uncertain.

polity.en: Safavid, Afsharid and Qajar Iran (Erivan Khanate)
polity.zh: 萨法维、阿夫沙尔与恺加伊朗（埃里温汗国）

polity.en: Russian Empire, then Republic of Armenia and Armenian SSR
polity.zh: 俄罗斯帝国，后为亚美尼亚共和国与亚美尼亚苏维埃共和国
亚美尼亚苏维埃社会主义共和国（苏联）

summary.en: Russia built a fortress at Gyumri and named it Alexandropol after the empress Alexandra Feodorovna. Renamed Leninakan in 1924, it was largely destroyed by the 1988 Spitak earthquake, briefly took back the old name Kumayri in 1990, and has been Gyumri since 1992.
summary.zh: 俄国在久姆里修建要塞，并以皇后亚历山德拉·费奥多罗芙娜之名命名为亚历山德罗波尔。1924年改名列宁纳坎，1988年斯皮塔克大地震中大半被毁，1990年短暂恢复古名库马伊里，1992年起称久姆里。

sources.title: G. A. Bournoutian, The Khanate of Erevan under Qajar Rule (1992)

note: The renaming to Alexandropol is dated 1837 (Nicholas I’s visit) or 1840; 1837 is used. Earlier names and pre-1555 rulers are omitted; Ottoman–Persian control alternated in the 16th–18th centuries.

polity.en: Roman Empire (after the partition of Armenia)
polity.zh: 罗马帝国（亚美尼亚分治后）
东罗马（拜占庭）帝国（约700–949年属阿拉伯）

polity.en: Sultanate of Rum, Ilkhanate, Turkmen dynasties
polity.zh: 罗姆苏丹国、伊利汗国、土库曼诸王朝

summary.en: Armenian Karin was fortified by Theodosius II as Theodosiopolis on the Roman–Persian frontier. Its Turkish name comes from Arabic Arzan al-Rum ("Arzan of the Romans"). In 1919 Mustafa Kemal held the Erzurum Congress here, a founding step of the Turkish national movement.
summary.zh: 亚美尼亚城市卡林被狄奥多西二世加固为罗马-波斯边境的狄奥多西奥波利斯。其土耳其名源自阿拉伯语“阿尔赞·鲁姆”（“罗马人的阿尔赞”）。1919年穆斯塔法·凯末尔在此召开埃尔祖鲁姆大会，是土耳其民族运动的奠基步骤之一。

sources.title: E. J. Zürcher, Turkey: A Modern History (3rd ed., 2004)

note: The refoundation as Theodosiopolis is dated c. 415–421; Seljuk takeover c. 1071–1080.
